_comment: Source of truth for published skill versions. Skills read this (cached daily, fail-silent) to tell users when an update is available. Bump the entry whenever you bump a skill's version.

changes: Copilot reviews work again on recent Copilot CLI versions (captured on 1.0.91; 1.0.90 failed the same way): 1.17.0 refused every Copilot answer because those CLIs add two events to the output MOMM reads. Older Copilot CLIs and other routes were not affected.
An answer returned inside one Markdown code fence is unwrapped and checked as strictly as before, on Copilot and Antigravity, by one shared rule; nothing is repaired.
A reviewer CLI that is too old for its configured model is flagged at preflight, before allowance is spent; MOMM makes no model call to find out and never changes your CLI settings.

Failures explain themselves: refusals name an unrecognised CLI event; a non-JSON answer leaves a private shape record; three identical failures in a row produce a notice; a refused evidence location prints one plain line with a safe remedy.
Updates stop before changing anything when a Git lock is present, and never remove it; a protocol change is summarised before the full diff; a Setup Center left running across an update says so.
The suite runner refuses unknown options, checks report storage first, ends with suites passed, report saved and exit status as three separate lines, and can recover a report that failed to save.

A fixture matrix runs each reviewer adapter against supported CLI versions; the local hygiene suite catches machine paths and credential-looking literals; the README and site carry one generated stable/candidate status line.

On macOS and Linux a reviewer CLI or Git found only inside the reviewed project is reported as not installed and never launched, as on Windows; the updater, probes and Setup Center helpers follow the same rule.

A .reviewrules file that arrives with a clone is ignored until you trust its exact hash; Codex reviews no longer load your MCP servers, global instructions or skills (your model and effort are read, never changed); Grok runs isolated for reviews, probes and pictures.
Capability probes are tied to the exact command that earned them, so an older MOMM never uses evidence it cannot act on; optional MOMM_EVIDENCE_HOME keeps evidence under your own profile.

Reviews that finish: readiness completes before dispatch, splitting keeps removals with their replacements, Grok pieces are capped at 20 KB and streamed, and a rejected quotation keeps a short private diagnostic.
Peer contract momm-peer-review/3: claim types, image observations anchored by hash and pixel region; versioned reviewer roles with an adversary loophole checklist; opt-in --cover and --second-look.
A stricter completion check: style rulings are checked against the bytes, optional mutation records, a stale-review notice, and a scorecard roster per route and role.
Guided picture rounds with consent and cost before each round, blind governor critique and a private gallery; update.mjs --release-claim recovers an interrupted upgrade.

A reviewed project can no longer choose the executable MOMM runs on Windows, or the Git that verifies a committed range on any platform; on macOS and Linux reviewer CLIs are still found through PATH (accepted risk, fix due in 1.17).
Committed-range reviews (--range) bind the report to both commits; capability expiry, retry evidence, failed-work accounting and tool-produced verification records.
Route failures quote the provider's own reason and never keep what MOMM sent, in any echo form.
A notice when a reviewer CLI is behind its latest release, with its update command, the off-by-default automatic option and the Setup Center.

Grok runs isolated from your Claude Code and Cursor setup and uses its faster serving when your account has it; Codex no longer reads the reviewed project's AGENTS.md or runs hooks, plugins, apps or multi-agent tools.
A reviewer's quotation counts when it differs only by typographic look-alikes or whitespace; every other character must still match.
The install prompt shows the standing-instructions section and waits for your yes before writing it.
Per-CLI token and cost accounting in every report, the ledger and the Setup Center usage panel.
Reviewer ratings with a five-run floor and 30-day route reliability that recommends only on ten or more runs.
Guidance layers (project, user, run) behind a per-file trust gate; untrusted guidance is never sent.

--split with per-piece quorum and --jobs parallel dispatch: a hunk larger than the ceiling is divided at line boundaries by default, and only a hunk that cannot be divided becomes governor-direct scope, listed in the report.
Event-driven update clock with conditional GETs; automatic updates are a toggle that is off by default and never enabled by an agent.
update --check-all, containment probes per CLI, and one design system with theme toggle shared by the Setup Center and the private ledger.

Modality registry and capability-aware routing: media attachments go only to routes whose capability is recorded, probes send synthetic material only and need consent, and an expired capability is blocked until re-probed.
Windows: the evidence folder is created private, `evidence --status | --protect` handles existing folders (owner-invoked), and Codex's read-only sandbox group on scratch is tolerated and recorded.
Windows launch guard: a git.exe or taskkill.exe planted in the reviewed project is never started; every process-launching script guards its own process.
Opt-in --retry-invalid: a review rejected as invalid output is re-sent once to the same route; off by default, validation never loosened, every retry disclosed in the report.
Fix signed updater staging discovery: gitsign needs a normal .git directory, with candidate files still unexecuted before verification.
Add a genuine signed-tag preview/apply gate before stable tag publication; retain all signature, hash and explicit consent checks.
Document 1.15.0 updater bootstrap and preserve the immutable original release.
Explicit check, signed preview, apply and offline previous-installation recovery; no automatic updates.
Per-harness installation receipts, stable/pinned/main channels and separate protocol acceptance.
DO_NOT_TRACK and once-daily notice handling; actual dispatcher, updater and protocol hashes in reports.
Focused information pages, attributed version archive, safe existing-user upgrade prompt and reconciled public evidence tables.
Source-bound governor completion with streamed append-only logs, explicit reviewer contract and cross-platform stability checks.
Visible FAQ, bounded review-output parsing and copyable evidence tables. Legacy unsigned release; not installable through the signature-enforcing updater.
Corrected public claims; evidence tables, prose corroboration, quick/deep tiers, invalid-output diagnostics and broader redaction.
Reconciled 1.10.x and installed 1.11/1.12 development; corrected supervisor timeouts and ledger speech.
Fixed narrow hydrated provider-card layouts and maintenance actions.
Corrective 1.10 packaging, responsive layout and stable terminal-exit fixture.
Provider authority, isolated setup probes, explicit connection states and OAuth environment policy.
Historical tag: Setup Center Host checks, stale verification, terminal errors and Windows timeout hardening.
Public code-history milestone, not a tagged release: loopback Setup Center and terminal onboarding.
Historical tag: cached daily version notices, opt-out and cache-path safeguards.
Historical tag: owner-only POSIX evidence permissions and surfaced ledger links.
Historical tag: prompt-file transport, redaction offsets and severity-merge fixes.
Public code-history milestone, not a tagged release: automatic private dashboard rebuild and ledger URL.
Public evidence Pages site and private per-workspace dashboards.
Five routes, personas, scaled timeouts, labels, quorum gates and stale-input detection.
Public code-history milestone, not a tagged release: setup hints, version/schema identity and Node guard.
multi-llm-review predecessor: OAuth peer reviews, governor self-exclusion and reproduction/disposition protocol. Original tag v0.1.0.
